title: Finite constant pro-etale sheaves are represented by labelled copies
statement: For a scheme U [def-pc-scheme] and a finite set E in the scheme universe, let U[E] be the disjoint union of copies of U indexed by E, as a weakly etale U-scheme. The canonical map from the constant sheaf with value ULift E [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] to the lifted representable sheaf h(U[E]) on [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] is an isomorphism. The map sends each constant label to that component, and these isomorphisms are natural in every map of finite label sets. Empty E is included.

source.place: Tag 0H7J, example-constant-sheaf; groupoids.tex Tag 03YW; proetale.tex Tag 098T. Adaptation of the proved ConstantSheafSetsRepresentable argument to pro-etale open coverings.

proof.text: The disjoint union is weakly etale since this is local at the source and each component is the identity. Construct the label-section map to its lifted representable sheaf. Subcanonicity supplies the sheaf condition.

A represented section determines a clopen partition by [lem-galois-coproduct-copies-morphisms-clopen]. The open pieces form a pro-etale cover, and on each piece the section is its label. If distinct labels coincide, the clopen preimage is both top and bottom, hence the domain is empty and its empty open covering proves local injectivity.

Sheafify the canonical section map. Both it and the sheafification unit are locally bijective, so the induced sheaf morphism is an isomorphism. Naturality follows by the sheafification adjunction, tested on constant labels, where it is the coproduct injection equation.
